a. [शूर्-अच्] Brave, heroic, valiant, mighty; शून्येषु शूरा न के [[K.

]]; स्वाध्यायशूरैर्मुखैः [[Pañch. 1. 5.]]

.]]

]])

.]]

a. One who fancies himself to be a hero.

.]]

-णखा (for नखा) ‘having finger-nails like winnowing-baskets’, N. of a sister of Rāvaṇa. [She was attracted by the beauty of Rāma and solicited him to marry her. But he said that as he had already got a wife she had better go to Lakṣmaṇa and try him. But he too rejected her, and back she came to Rāma. This circumstance excited Sītā's laughter, and the revengeful demoness, feeling herself grossly insulted, assumed a hideous form and threatened to eat her up. But Lakṣmaṇa cut off her ears and nose, and thus doubly deformed her; see [[

-40.]]] 
-वातः wind produced by shaking a winnowing-basket.

.]]

__1 an epithet of Bṛhaspati; धर्मः शास्त्रं सुरगुरुमतिः शौचमाचारचिन्ता सस्यैः पूर्णे जठरपिठरे प्राणिनां संभवन्ति [[

.]]

.]]

-र्मी f.

[सरति आकाशे सूर्यः, यद्वा सुवति कर्मणि लोकं प्रेरयति; cf. [[Sk.]] on [[

]]] 
__1 The sun; सूर्ये तपत्यावरणाय दृष्टेः कल्पेत लोकस्य कथं तमिस्रा [[

.]] [In mythology, the sun is regarded as a son of Kaśyapa and Aditi. He is represented as moving in a chariot drawn by seven horses, with Aruṇa for his charioteer. He is also represented as all-seeing, the constant beholder of the good and bad deeds of mortals. Samjñā (or Chāyā or Aśvinī) was his principal wife, by whom he had Yama and Yamunā, the two Aśvins and Saturn. He is also described as having been the father of Manu Vaivasvata, the founder of the solar race of kings.] 
__2 The tree called Arka. 
__3 The number ‘twelve’ (derived from the twelve forms of the sun). 
__4 The swallow-wort. 
__5 N. of Śiva.
